extracted.intended_audience: interested parties and the public (e.g., commenters, counsel, stakeholders in hazardous materials transport and tort claimants/defendants)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and legal standards for submitting public comments on a PHMSA application for an administrative determination whether Federal hazardous material transportation law (49 U.S.C. 5125) preempts certain state common law tort claims. Includes procedural requirements for comments and the substantive preemption criteria PHMSA will apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments should be directed to whether 49 U.S.C. 5125 preempts state common law tort claims regarding the marking, hazardous material employee training, loading and unloading, and hazardous material classification for gasoline transported by cargo tank motor vehicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should specifically address the preemption criteria discussed in Part II of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment deadlines and rebuttal limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments received on or before February 9, 2026 and rebuttal comments received on or before March 10, 2026 will be considered before an administrative determination is issued by PHMSA's Chief Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any rebuttal comments may only discuss issues raised by comments received during the initial comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file comments and docket reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must refer to Docket No. PHMSA-2025-0777 and may be submitted via Regulations.gov, fax (1-202-493-2251), mail, or hand delivery to the Docket Operations Facility (M-30), U.S. Department of Transportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online instructions on Regulations.gov. When mailing/hand-delivering, use the specified address and office hours. Use the docket number in submissions to ensure placement in the correct file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirement and certification of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters must send a copy of their comment to the individuals listed in the notice (Exxon's counsel and listed attorneys/judges) and must include a certification that a copy of the comment has been sent to these persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice lists specific persons and addresses (Ilana H. Eisenstein; The Honorable Bruce J. Kaplan; Andrew J. Dupont; Jeffrey Kluger). Failure to certify service may affect procedural fairness or record completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting and privacy of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: DOT posts comments, without edit, including any personal information the commenter provides, to https://www.regulations.gov, as described in the system of records notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual compliance test (49 U.S.C. 5125(a) — "not possible" standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-Federal requirement is preempted if complying with the non-Federal requirement and the Federal requirement is not possible (the 'dual compliance' criterion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dual compliance criterion derives from 49 U.S.C. 5125(a) and Supreme Court decisions; if it is impossible to comply with both the state and federal requirement, the state requirement is preempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obstacle test (49 U.S.C. 5125(a) — 'obstacle' standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-Federal requirement is preempted if, as applied and enforced, it is an obstacle to accomplishing and carrying out the Federal requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA applies an 'obstacle' analysis to determine whether the state requirement interferes with federal objectives under the hazardous materials transportation law.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Substantively the same" standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-Federal requirement concerning certain enumerated subjects is preempted unless it is 'substantively the same' as a provision of Federal hazardous material transportation law, a regulation prescribed under that law, or a relevant DHS hazardous materials security regulation or directive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be 'substantively the same,' the non-Federal requirement must conform 'in every significant respect' to the Federal requirement; editorial and other similar de minimis changes are permitted. (See citation to 49 CFR 107.202(d) / 49 U.S.C. 5125(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject area: designation, description, and classification of hazardous material
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Federal requirements concerning 'the designation, description, and classification of hazardous material' are preempted when not substantively the same as Federal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA will compare state-level classification or reclassification demands (e.g., reclassifying gasoline from Class 3 to Class 6.1) against federal classification schemes to determine whether they are substantively the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject area: packing, repacking, handling, labeling, marking, and placarding
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Federal requirements concerning 'the packing, repacking, handling, labeling, marking, and placarding of hazardous material' are preempted when not substantively the same as Federal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subject area encompasses duties a state tort claim might impose (e.g., special marking or warnings about benzene). PHMSA will evaluate whether such state obligations differ in any significant respect from the HMR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject area: shipping documents (preparation, execution, use, number/contents/placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Federal requirements concerning 'the preparation, execution, and use of shipping documents related to hazardous material and requirements related to the number, contents, and placement of those documents' are preempted when not substantively the same as Federal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State requirements that would change shipping paper content, placement, or execution will be contrasted with HMR shipping document requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject area: written notification/recording/reporting of unintentional releases and incident reporting involving State/local emergency responders
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Federal requirements concerning 'the written notification, recording, and reporting of the unintentional release in transportation of hazardous material and other written hazardous materials transportation incident reporting involving State or local emergency responders in the initial response to the incident' are preempted when not substantively the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHMSA will review state incident reporting or notification requirements to determine whether they conflict with or duplicate federal reporting standards for initial response by emergency responders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject area: design/manufacturing/inspection/maintenance/etc. of packaging represented as qualified for transport
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Federal requirements concerning 'the designing, manufacturing, fabricating, inspecting, marking, maintaining, reconditioning, repairing, or testing a package, container, or packaging component that is represented, marked, certified, or sold as qualified for use in transporting hazardous material in commerce' are preempted when not substantively the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers state rules affecting packaging and qualification standards for transportable containers; PHMSA will compare them to federal packaging and qualification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption determination process and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person directly affected by a State/local/tribal requirement may apply to the Secretary of Transportation (delegated to PHMSA) for a determination whether the requirement is preempted; the application is noticed in the Federal Register, PHMSA considers written comments, publishes its determination, allows a short period for petitions for reconsideration, and a petition for judicial review must be filed in the D.C. Circuit or the petitioner's circuit within 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process steps: file application, publication of notice, comment period, PHMSA determination in Federal Register, short reconsideration window, judicial review timeline and venues (49 U.S.C. 5127(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of federalism and preemption policy
rubrics_metrics.description: In making preemption determinations under 49 U.S.C. 5125(d), PHMSA will consider principles and policies set forth in Executive Order 13132 (Federalism) and the May 20, 2009 Presidential Memorandum on Preemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 4(a) of E.O. 13132 and the Memorandum emphasize that preemption should be undertaken only with full consideration of States' prerogatives and a sufficient legal basis; express preemption, clear congressional intent, or direct conflict are required bases for preemption under these policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitations of PHMSA preemption determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Preemption determinations do not address preemption arising under the Commerce Clause, the Fifth Amendment, other constitutional provisions, or statutes other than the Federal hazardous material transportation law unless necessary to determine whether a requirement is authorized by another Federal law or whether a fee is 'fair' under 49 U.S.C. 5125(f)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State/local requirements are not deemed authorized by another Federal law merely because they are not preempted by another Federal statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory definitions relevant to preemption analysis (example: 'loading incidental to movement')
rubrics_metrics.description: For bulk packaging, 'loading incidental to movement is filling the packaging with a hazardous material for the purpose of transporting it when performed by carrier personnel or in the presence of carrier personnel...' (49 CFR 171.1(c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretive definitions in the HMR (e.g., 'loading incidental to movement') are applied to determine whether state duties (e.g., regarding loading arms or loading practices) fall within federally regulated activity and thus are subject to preemption analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of application and docket materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The application (Exxon Preemption Application with Exhibits 1-7) and all comments are available on the U.S. Government Regulations.gov website and at the Docket Operations Facility address provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested parties may review the application, exhibits (including the New Jersey state court opinion included as Exhibit 1), and submitted comments in the docket to inform their own comments or responses.
